# Synopsys (SNPS): company research and funded operating valuation

**Version 3 | information cutoff: October 18, 2026 | financial origin: July 31, 2026**

## Decision summary

Synopsys has a strong engineering-software franchise, an expanded simulation portfolio and a credible opportunity to charge for more of the work performed by its tools. The investment case nevertheless depends on execution after an unusually large acquisition, a recovery in IP, and converting AI enthusiasm into profitable contracts. Its headline growth, adjusted profitability and cash flow each need substantial qualification.

The grant-normalized analyst DCF produces July-origin operating enterprise values of **$17.48B downside, $44.82B base and $79.72B upside**. The explicit default claim and inventory assumptions produce **conditional July-origin values of $50.10, $188.12 and $364.31 per common share**, respectively. Claim-allowance adequacy and award completeness are unverified; these amounts are not verified July values or October targets. These are scenario estimates, not current market targets. They retain R&D and future stock grants as economic expenses, fund incremental growth and terminal reinvestment, and include the remaining cash payment on already-accrued restructuring.

**Unqualified common-equity value and current-price comparison remain gated.** Conditional dated allocation is now available, with visible assumptions. Exact July award allocation, legacy claims and the July-to-October capital bridge remain incomplete. The October $1B accelerated repurchase cannot be reflected only in the denominator. The v2 operating research and historical corrections passed independent review. The new v3 compensation and allocation work is submitted for independent research review; it does not authorize import or publication.

## 1. Security, dates and source discipline

The [official US Robinhood page](https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/SNPS/) identifies Synopsys, Inc. and SNPS. The [July 2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000025/snps-20260731.htm), cover, confirms common stock, $0.01 par value, on Nasdaq Global Select Market; CIK 0000883241. This establishes security identity and a public brokerage listing, not eligibility in a particular user's account. The Robinhood snapshot labels October 18, a Sunday, with intraday wording. No quote, market capitalization or share-price regression enters this valuation.

The last available financial statement is July 31, 2026, filed August 26. September 30 Investor Day guidance and October 5 repurchase terms are information available at the cutoff. They are not July balance-sheet cash. The discount assumptions use October opportunity costs, so the result is a July-origin reconstruction using later information, rather than a contemporaneous July appraisal.

The source ledger records original URLs, retrieval timestamps and SHA-256 hashes. Annual filings for FY2016–2025, quarterly statements, dated releases, official prepared remarks, supplements, the 2026 proxy and the 119-page Investor Day deck are retained privately. Third-party call/interview transcripts are used only for limited attribution and cross-checks; neither their full text nor raw company documents are in the public-safe bundle.

## 2. How the business earns revenue

Design Automation combines EDA software, hardware-assisted verification, system tools and Ansys simulation. Design IP supplies reusable circuit designs and related customization. Customers buy shorter development time, lower failure risk and confidence that complex designs can be manufactured. Switching requires workflow qualification, trained engineers, foundry support and design-history compatibility. These are strong barriers, but they do not eliminate pricing negotiations, alternatives or customer bargaining power.

Q3 revenue was $2.476822B: Design Automation $2.002971B and Design IP $473.851M. The product view was approximately $1.2825B EDA, $711.1M Ansys, $473.8M IP and $9.3M Other. Those rounded product values are allocations, not independently audited segment profits. Segment adjusted operating income was $905.028M and $125.392M. The combined $1.030420B reconciles to only $357.491M GAAP EBIT after acquired amortization, SBC, restructuring, transaction items and deferred-compensation market movements. [10-Q, Note 17](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000025/snps-20260731.htm).

Recognition categories were $1.002792B time-based products, $665.223M upfront products and $808.807M maintenance/services. The [official supplement](https://s201.q4cdn.com/778493406/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/supplemental-info/Synopsys-Q3-FY2026-Financial-Supplement-Updated.pdf), pp. 2–3, calls 82% recurring, defined as time-based products, multi-period IP contracts, and maintenance/services recognized over time. **This is not ARR.** There is no defensible consolidated ARR figure in the reviewed materials. A quarterly recurring-revenue percentage cannot establish an annualized renewal base or retention rate.

A license sale, a contracted obligation, a billing and a cash receipt are different events. EDA term arrangements can recognize ratably; hardware and certain licenses can recognize upfront; maintenance and services can be ratable or recognized as performed. IP obligations can depend on development milestones and specific deliverables. Royalties depend on later customer sales. Product-group growth consequently cannot be read as a simple subscription-seat metric.

### Backlog and cash conversion

July backlog was approximately $10.9B, including $1.9B noncancelable flexible-spending commitments without final product selection. Of the other $9B, 49% is expected in the next 12 months: **$4.41B**, not 49% of $10.9B. Future sales-based royalties are excluded. Contract assets were $1.230279B, unbilled receivables $31.864M and deferred revenue $2.715109B. Nine-month sales-based royalty revenue was $89.8M. [10-Q, Note 5](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000025/snps-20260731.htm).

Backlog fell from $11.4B at October 2025 to $10.9B. Contract duration, consumption, acquisition/perimeter changes and the Processor IP sale matter. The [August prepared remarks](https://s201.q4cdn.com/778493406/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/transcript/SNPS_Q326_Prepared_Remarks.pdf), pp. 5–6, attribute a modest sequential decline to that sale. The balance is neither ARR nor guaranteed next-year revenue, and its movement alone does not prove demand deterioration.

Ansys channel accounting changed in Q2 2026: $12.5M of revenue and matching expense were grossed up, with an estimated $60M FY2026 impact and no EPS or cash-flow benefit. This mechanically lifts revenue and dilutes margin percentage. The May revenue-guidance increase comprised $35M improved performance, $60M gross presentation and a $40M Processor IP divestiture reduction. Treating the full change as organic growth would be wrong. [May prepared remarks](https://s201.q4cdn.com/778493406/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/transcript/SNPS_Q226_Prepared_Remarks.pdf), pp. 5–6.

## 3. Strategy, management evidence and what would validate it

The current management team is CEO Sassine Ghazi and CFO Shelagh Glaser. Official Q3 remarks describe stronger EDA, an IP return to growth, the first Multiphysics Fusion products and more than 30 active agentic-AI customer engagements. Those are operational indicators, not disclosed incremental AI revenue. Q3 EDA grew 8.5%, while management expected double-digit Q4 and full-year growth. IP grew about 11% in Q3, but nine-month IP revenue remained slightly below the prior year and adjusted segment income declined from $363.084M to $302.170M. A recovery is underway; it is not yet demonstrated across the whole year.

The [September 30 official Investor Day deck](https://s201.q4cdn.com/778493406/files/doc_presentations/2026/2026-09-30-Investor-Day_Presentation_All_Final.pdf) provides the clearest forward framework:

- FY2026–FY2030 company revenue CAGR around 15%; EDA 13%+, simulation/analysis 10%+, IP 17%+. These are management objectives, not contracted growth.
- Approximately $400M annualized revenue synergies by FY2029 and $400M annualized cost synergies by FY2027, the latter one year earlier than the original target. A run rate is not cumulative realized cash.
- Approximately 50% adjusted operating margin and SBC near 8% of revenue by FY2030. The natural owner-profit starting point is therefore about 42%, before retained restructuring or other economic exclusions.
- Mid-20% EPS and FCF growth; up to 50% of FCF returned through repurchases. Buybacks are capital allocation, not an operating-value multiplier.
- Application-optimized IP targeted at approximately $1B by FY2030, with royalty mix expected to become larger than license fees over time. Product development, customer concentration and design-to-production timing remain risks.

The [Amazon agreement](https://news.synopsys.com/2026-09-30-Synopsys-and-Amazon-Announce-Strategic%2C-Multi-year-IP-Agreement-for-Custom-Silicon-Collaboration-Also-Extends-to-Cloud-and-AI-Powered-Engineering) is multi-year and described as $1B+, moving toward license-plus-royalty economics. Its announcement does not authorize recognizing $1B of immediate revenue or cash. Synopsys also becomes a greater AWS consumer, so commercial upside and compute spending should both be considered. The [OpenAI partnership](https://news.synopsys.com/2026-09-30-OpenAI-and-Synopsys-Announce-GPT-Synopsys-Frontier-Intelligence-to-Revolutionize-Chip-Design) introduces a joint model/workflow initiative, not disclosed stand-alone revenue or a quantified margin contribution.

At the [June 9 Mizuho interview](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/snps/transcripts/679795-mizuho-technology-conference-2026/), Ghazi emphasized annual rather than quarterly EDA comparisons because hardware is lumpy, acknowledged portfolio-comparison complexity, and described a move toward IP royalties. This is useful evidence of the strategic rationale; it is not independent proof of demand. At the [September Investor Day Q&A](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/snps/transcripts/682621-investor-day-2026/), management clarified that the Amazon license commitment and future royalties are distinct, and royalty growth develops after FY2027. Exact customer terms were not disclosed. Public conclusions here rely primarily on the official deck and releases.

Monitor actual organic EDA growth, IP revenue and margin, Ansys cross-selling, recognized AI/AOIP revenue, gross-versus-net consistency, customer acceptance and cash collection. The downside becomes more likely if growing design workloads fail to produce pricing or consumption revenue, if custom-IP engineering absorbs the royalty upside, or if restrictions prevent delivery to important customers.

Important breaks:

1. FY2018 and FY2024 have 53 weeks. FY2025 changed to an actual October 31 year-end and had 363 days, beginning November 3, 2024. Older filings label periods with the nearest calendar month-end; the JSON retains actual dates separately.
2. ASC606 and commission capitalization began in FY2019 using modified retrospective adoption. Earlier years were not restated. The issuer's FY2019 old-standard comparison was revenue $3.258163B and EBIT $413.579M versus reported $3.360694B and $520.231M. The apparent acceleration is not wholly economic. Lease accounting changed subsequently; balance-sheet capital ratios need that label.
3. Black Duck, WhiteHat and other acquisitions built Software Integrity. That business was sold September 30, 2024 and removed from comparative continuing P&L in FY2022–2023. The historical cash and income statements do not share one uninterrupted perimeter. The sale gain is not recurring operating earnings.
4. The FY2023 product taxonomy moved activities from the old IP/System Integration category into EDA and other categories. FY2022 EDA appears as 50.8% in its original taxonomy and 62.9% in the later recast. These must not be spliced. FY2027 introduces another reclassification: Ansys semiconductor tools and Other move into EDA; residual Ansys becomes S&A, while the two reportable segments remain unchanged.
5. Ansys closed July 17, 2025 and contributed $756.6M in FY2025. FY2026 includes a full year. Optical Solutions/PowerArtist, OpenLight and Processor IP dispositions further affect comparisons. The Ansys purchase price of $34.858480B includes cash, stock, pre-combination awards and pre-existing relationships; historical acquisition cash alone understates economic investment.
6. Original FY2024 net capex was $123.161M. The FY2025 filing's comparative is $139.500M; the continuing-operations IR series is about $121.7M. These conflicting versions are retained and flagged, not silently reconciled or called organic reinvestment. The generic XBRL amortization series has varying scope: older note totals can include capitalized-software amortization, whereas later tags can cover only the operating-expense row. It is now named amortization_of_intangible_assets_xbrl_scope_varies, with period-specific scope. Only the separately validated sum of cost-of-revenue and operating-expense acquired-intangible rows is the acquisition-only P&L add-back.
7. Shares/EPS retain issuer-reported units. No extra split factor is imposed. A weighted-average diluted denominator is not converted into a current legal share count.

## 5. Guidance versus actual outcomes

The record supports a capable company, but not an unconditional “always beats” thesis. The machine-readable scorecard preserves original, reset and latest guidance separately.

- **FY2023:** initial revenue $5.775–5.825B versus $5.842619B; adjusted EPS $10.28–10.35 versus $11.19; GAAP EPS $7.68–7.86 versus $7.92. CFO approximately $1.7B versus $1.703274B. This is a comparatively clean positive year. [Initial release](https://news.synopsys.com/2022-11-30-Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2022).
- **FY2024:** original $6.570–6.630B revenue included Software Integrity and cannot be scored against $6.127436B continuing revenue. The May continuing reset was $6.090–6.150B, within which actual fell, while adjusted EPS exceeded the reset range. Final August GAAP EPS guidance was $9.71–9.85, but continuing actual was $9.25; adjusted EPS was $13.20. [May reset](https://investor.synopsys.com/news/news-details/2024/Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2024/default.aspx), [year-end results](https://investor.synopsys.com/news/news-details/2024/Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024/default.aspx).
- **FY2025:** original revenue $6.745–6.805B excluded Ansys. Combined actual $7.054178B is not an organic beat: subtracting disclosed Ansys contribution gives a legacy proxy $6.297578B, about 7% below the original midpoint, with divestiture qualifications. The September combined reset was $7.030–7.060B and adjusted EPS $12.76–12.80; actual revenue was inside that range and adjusted EPS $12.91 exceeded it. Initial EPS is not cleanly comparable after acquisition financing and share issuance. [Initial guide](https://investor.synopsys.com/news/news-details/2024/Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024/default.aspx), [FY2025 actual](https://investor.synopsys.com/news/news-details/2025/Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2025/default.aspx).
- **Q2 FY2026:** revenue $2.275970B just exceeded the prior $2.275B high end, but included the $12.5M presentation gross-up; excluding it, revenue was within range. Adjusted EPS $3.35 beat $3.11–3.17, while GAAP EPS $0.09 missed $0.23–0.43 because restructuring accelerated.
- **Q3 FY2026:** revenue $2.476822B beat $2.410–2.460B and adjusted EPS $3.91 beat $3.63–3.69. GAAP EPS $2.84 includes the Processor IP sale gain; it is not a normal quarterly run rate. [August release](https://news.synopsys.com/2026-08-26-Synopsys-Posts-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026).

FY2026 revenue midpoint rose from $9.610B in December to $9.715B in August; adjusted EPS midpoint rose from $14.36 to $15.07. CFO guidance rose from $2.2B to $2.8B, while capex fell from $300M to $225M. Rounded FCF guidance of $2.6B is not the exact $2.575B arithmetic difference.

September's FY2027 guidance is $11.1–11.2B revenue, $19.04–19.12 adjusted EPS, approximately 44% adjusted operating margin, $3.6B CFO, $500M capex and $3.1B FCF. GAAP expense guidance is $8.765–8.905B, including $1.540–1.550B acquired amortization, $960–980M SBC and $50–100M restructuring. [Official Investor Day release](https://news.synopsys.com/2026-09-30-Synopsys-Details-Growth-Strategy-and-Long-term-Financial-Model-at-2026-Investor-Day).

## 6. Conditional dated capital and award allocation

### Reported July balances and assumed asset recoveries

The origin is July 31, 2026. Unrestricted cash is $3.606286B, short-term investments $1.383M and public equity $0.684M. Restricted cash of $4.490M is excluded. A $291.450M operating cash reserve leaves $3.314836B before distribution/availability adjustments. The base assumes that excess cash has the reported rounded 46% foreign mix and applies a 10% haircut to that portion, reducing credit by $152.482M to $3.162354B. This is an analyst valuation haircut, not a measured tax bill or proof of distributability. Liquid investments receive 75% recovery, or $1.550M. Private investments and the $22.202M Software Integrity contingent receivable receive zero credit; its $475M contractual maximum is not an asset valuation.

Debt principal is $10.110449B, including the $99.526M treasury-lock deferred settlement and $10.923M other borrowings. The treasury-lock item is already in total debt. The separate $170.462M accrued interest and $88.454M current-tax accrual are also deducted. Forward unlevered profit excludes financing interest, and normalized forecast taxes fund post-origin earnings. The model excludes income taxes from operating-capital investment and does not schedule a second settlement of the opening tax accrual. [July 10-Q, Notes 7–11](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000025/snps-20260731.htm).

The cash-flow bridge still reconciles opening cash including restricted cash of $2.893721B, plus $2.298603B CFO and $353.763M CFI, less $1.901902B financing cash and $33.409M FX, to $3.610776B. Closed Ansys financing, the processor-IP divestiture and NVIDIA's $2B placement are already reflected. They are not funded or credited again.

### Residual claims: a visible allowance, not a verified bound

The base deducts a further **$350M residual non-operating allowance**. Its components are $200M for legacy uncertain-tax, pension and acquired obligations; $75M for other unmatched legacy retention, contingent or minority claims; and $75M headroom. The references are July's $215.654M other noncurrent accruals, after separately identifying deferred tax and matched deferred compensation, and the prior annual $173.734M gross uncertain-tax balance plus $0.9M interest/penalties. These references overlap and are not additive. They do not prove the actual net cash settlement.

The allowance excludes the separately deducted debt, interest and current-tax accrual. It also excludes ordinary payroll, trade payables, deferred revenue, recurring service/retention cost and operating leases already funded through operating costs/NWC. The full $837.594M payroll accrual, $187.322M trade payables, $196.766M other current accruals and $215.654M noncurrent other balance are not added as extra debt. Their operating/non-operating composition is not sufficiently disaggregated to justify doing so.

The $471.484M deferred-compensation asset and matched liability are excluded together. Operating rent remains expensed, so the $804.429M lease liability is not also deducted. Neither the $95.515M DTA nor the $850.250M DTL is mechanically added/subtracted on top of assumed cash taxes. Korean withholding-tax claims can have foreign-tax-credit offsets. The $20.401M FX derivative liability is handled within operating cash assumptions; an optional extra-claim stress applies only if it represents an unfunded non-operating settlement. Opening restructuring of $64.9M is paid once in Q4 FCFF and excluded from the residual allowance.

The $350M allowance is conditional. It is not a reported balance, completeness-certified estimate or upper bound. Stress amounts of $200M/$350M/$700M are analyst intervals, not confidence bounds. Litigation, pension, minority claims or acquisition obligations may exceed them. Cash-tax runoff and precise claim overlap remain open inputs.

### Issued shares, unissued awards and the acquired cohort

July legal common shares are 191.605M, reconciled from 185.994M by NVIDIA issuance, net employee/acquisition issuance and repurchases. Q3 weighted-average diluted shares of 192.319M are not a dated denominator.

The [FY2025 annual filing, Note 15](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324125000028/snps-20251031.htm), gives October 31, 2025 all-plan counts of **4.318M unissued RSUs**, including maximum performance conditions, and **1.154M options** with $357.66 weighted strike and 3.74-year remaining life. Approximately 0.006M directors' restricted shares are already-issued stock, rather than RSUs; they are not added again to legal common. The [proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000007/snps-20260219.htm), page 95, has a narrower 4.423M plan-table total and separately excludes about 0.895M acquired Ansys RSUs and 235 other acquired options. Its combined 5.318235M is below the annual all-plan RSU-plus-option total of 5.472M. Plan/performance-count conventions differ; the full 0.153765M difference is not reconciled. The broader annual maximum-condition counts are selected, without adding that difference as another award cohort.

The 4.318M RSU total already includes Ansys replacement units. At closing, 1.116M RSUs and about 0.005M options were assumed in Synopsys share units; the remaining acquired cohort is a subset of later totals. The [closing 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000114036125026139/ef20051970_8k.htm) distinguishes common consideration of 0.3399 Synopsys shares plus $199.91 cash from award conversion: 0.3399 plus $199.91 divided by the five-trading-day Synopsys VWAP ending July 16, 2025. The published Synopsys-unit inventory is already converted and must not be multiplied by either ratio again. Continuing assumed performance awards became service-based; specified vested/director/departed-employee awards settled in merger consideration instead.

The $639.7M acquisition-date award fair value included $130.963M pre-combination consideration and approximately $508.7M post-combination service cost. These are accounting allocations, not additional cash claims to stack on top of the funded acquisition and full existing-award allocation. No extra 0.895M acquired RSU count or $639.7M cash deduction is applied.

The base explicitly **assumes those October inventory quantities persist at July** after unknown grants, vesting and forfeitures. This is not a factual roll-forward. Existing ESPP rights are assumed at 1.0M units, approximately two years of recent 0.5M annual purchase volume across overlapping offerings. Actual active rights are not disclosed. Full participation is assigned to all assumed RSUs, options and ESPP rights, with zero exercise-proceeds credit. This is a full-share allocation convention, not option fair value. For a fixed inventory it can overallocate option/ESPP participation, but it does not prove that the inventory is complete.

The default denominator is **191.605 + 4.318 + 1.154 + 1.000 = 198.077M units**. The pool is operating EV plus $3.162354B cash and $1.550M liquid investments, less $10.110449B debt, $170.462M interest, $88.454M current tax and $350M residual claims. The pool is allocated jointly between legal common and assumed unissued awards. No future-grant units, issued restricted stock, option value or exercise proceeds are added separately. Each additional $100M net claim changes the default value by about $0.505 per share.

### The post-origin ASR

The [October 5 ASR](https://news.synopsys.com/2026-10-05-Synopsys-Initiates-1-Billion-Accelerated-Share-Repurchase-Agreement) has a $1B commitment, expected initial delivery of approximately 1.735M shares, and final settlement by January 5, 2027. It is completely excluded from the July cash balance, July allocation units and unlevered operating FCFF. A current-date case must match actual payment, delivery, residual forward and all intervening cash/share movements. There is no assumed final share count derived from a current stock price.

## 7. Future grants, funded DCF and sensitivities

### Compensation that remains an economic expense

Approximate gross new-grant value proxies are $931.218M, $1,014.535M and $758.146M for FY2023–2025. They combine RSU grants times weighted grant-date value, option grants times option value, directors' restricted-stock grants and ESPP purchases times purchase-right value. Acquired replacement awards are excluded from new-grant counts. Matched broad reported revenue gives 15.94%, 15.38% and 10.75%; FY2024 includes $468.720M discontinued revenue because its award scope includes that business. These are approximate gross proxies before forfeitures, with maximum performance units and rounded ESPP purchase cohorts, not exact expected grant values or accounting SBC.

FY2025's $758.146M divided by revenue excluding the $756.6M acquired Ansys stub gives 12.04%, but is only a perimeter sensitivity because post-close grant recipients cannot be separated. Separately, [Ansys's FY2024 filing, Note 15](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1013462/000101346225000009/anss-20241231.htm), gives 0.948M new RSUs at $339.43 weighted grant-date value: $321.780M, or 12.64% of $2.544809B revenue. That standalone RSU-only proxy excludes ESPP and reflects a pending-merger year without market-condition grants. It is not a fabricated consolidated grant series.

The analyst selects future new-grant cost at **15% downside, 12% base and 10% upside** of revenue. The base is near the recent perimeter and Ansys references; the downside reflects older higher grant intensity, while the upside requires lower grant intensity. Management's 8–9% accounting-SBC outlook is not proof of the cost of future grants. A separate 8–15% sensitivity holds pre-SBC margins fixed; lower grant costs cannot be hidden by an offsetting rise in other costs.

For Q4, start with direct GAAP guidance plus acquired amortization. Remove the selected accounting SBC of $240M/$235M/$230M, then charge economic new grants. Base EBIT is **$695M + $235M − $306.6M = $623.4M**. This is a replacement, not free SBC. For FY2027, base EBIT is **$3.860B + $970M − $1.338B = $3.492B**, a 31.32% margin. R&D, restructuring and integration costs remain expensed. Later base economic margins reach 34.5% in FY2030 and 35% thereafter.

Already-granted awards receive the separate participation allocation. July's $1.4B unrecognized options/RSU/restricted-stock expense and $105.6M ESPP expense are not extra cash deductions or automatic PV credits. A diagnostic straight-line recognition schedule subtracts and reverses identical legacy expense; changing its timing has zero effect on valuation. Full legacy allocation is used once, while future grants are expensed and are not also added to future shares. No separate vesting tax windfall is assumed.

For functional-cost display, 50% of the change in grant expense is allocated to R&D, close to FY2025 R&D's 51.14% share of reported SBC. This is a composition assumption. The full cost is already deducted in EBIT, and R&D and grants overlap; do not sum or subtract them twice.

### Forecast and investment

The executable model retains the July 31 origin, exact ACT/365.25 period-end dates, Q4 stub and ten fiscal years. Prior nine-month cash flows are not valued again. Direct Q4 guidance remains the profit anchor because full-year and quarterly guidance components do not perfectly reconcile; v2's pre-normalization $36.654M EBIT discrepancy is retained as a source issue rather than erased.

All per-share rows assume 198.077M allocation units and the disclosed claim/asset assumptions; they are not company-value bounds or October price targets.

Q4 retains capex of $68.911M less ordinary D&A of $50.576M, plus 8% of positive sequential growth for operating capital and $64.9M legacy restructuring cash. Base Q4 FCFF is $384.295M. Annual reinvestment is positive revenue growth times the new economic margin and after-tax retention, divided by the declining incremental return, subject to the FY2027 capex/NWC floor. Base FY2027 net investment is $682.353M, above the $404.672M floor; FCFF is $1.971567B. Lower profit margins reduce investment under this specified return-based policy, while the physical capex floor remains. This is a funded analyst model, not independently proven capacity economics.

The default attributes margin expansion to productivity/integration funded through expensed R&D and restructuring. A separate stress funds all positive NOPAT growth, using a like-for-like normalized FY2026 profit reference only for investment calculation. Operating EV becomes approximately $17.015B/$43.230B/$77.741B. No historical cash flow is created or revalued in that reference calculation.

Discount rates, growth and terminal-return assumptions are unchanged from v2. The base WACC evidence remains the October 16 Treasury 5.09% yield, October 1 implied ERP 4.20% and January software cash-adjusted asset beta 1.25. Analyst leverage/spread/tax assumptions produce 10.03368%, with 10.5% selected. No current share-price input is used. The separate cost-of-capital file retains original source links and dates.

Base FY2027 NOPAT of $2.653920B is about 6.99% of the unchanged $37.945609B acquisition-inclusive opening capital diagnostic. The later 12% terminal incremental return still requires execution. Do not remove goodwill to manufacture high returns. Terminal reinvestment remains g/ROIC, and downside growth at 8% ROIC below 12% WACC destroys value relative to capital cost. The 45-cell WACC/g/ROIC grid, grant-cost grid, residual-claim/award grid and individual capital sensitivities are included.

## 8. Review gates and handoff

Before unqualified common-equity or current-price use:

1. Reconcile exact dated award cohorts, strikes, vesting, performance conditions, service expense and earned claims, including assumed Ansys awards and ESPP.
2. Complete July-to-October cash/debt/shares/claims movement, including ASR payment, delivery and residual settlement. Do not roll forward with accounting EPS shares.
3. Resolve availability/tax leakage of cash and investment credits, and same-date legacy tax, pension, litigation and contingent consideration classifications.
4. Validate scenario cash taxes, ordinary D&A and working-capital funding against a detailed schedule, especially the Ansys purchase-accounting tax basis and AOIP/cloud spending.
5. Resolve historical source conflicts and product reclassifications before calculating continuous organic growth, capital turnover or management hit rates.

Internal checks cover arithmetic, dated periods, source integrity, cash/share/debt reconciliation, guidance bridges, retained expenses and funded terminal value. They are not external approval. No app edits or publishing were performed.
